title: Lists and shopping lists
subtitle: A list stores items in order. Read them by position or process them one by one.
concept: A list stores items in order. Read them by position or process them one by one.
intuition: A shopping list has a first and second item, and you can add another at the end.
objectives: Two names can refer to one list

body.title: Put items inside square brackets
body.text: items = ["apple", "bread"] creates a list with two strings, separated by a comma inside square brackets. Lists preserve order. items[0] retrieves the first item; items[1] retrieves the second. Positions start at 0. len(items) gives the number of items, here 2.

body.title: Append an item, then iterate
body.text: items.append("milk") adds an item at the end. The dot selects an operation on this list; append is its name. for item in items: visits each item directly, without a range or an index.

body.title: Two names can refer to one list
body.text: other = items does not copy the list. It gives the same list another name, so appending through other also changes what items sees. For independent simple lists, use other = items.copy(). This is a shallow copy; here the list contains only strings or numbers.

formalDefinition.text: Lists preserve order and duplicates, and positions start at 0. append adds at the end; copy duplicates the simple, one-level lists used here.
conditions: An index must be within the list. An empty list has no item at index 0.
Here copy() is used on one-level lists of numbers or strings.

derivation.text: The first item is at index 0.
for visits items in their list order.
apple therefore prints once on its own and again during iteration.

interactiveVisual.prediction: After an append, what is the order?

workedExamples.title: Read a shopping list
workedExamples.problem: Read the first item, then print every item.
steps: The first item is at index 0.
for visits items in their list order.
apple therefore prints once on its own and again during iteration.

answer.code:
items = ["apple", "bread"]
print(items[0])
for item in items:
    print(item)

workedExamples.title: Add milk
workedExamples.problem: Append an item and print the new length.
steps: The list starts with two items.

commonMistakes.claim: The first item is at position 1.
commonMistakes.correction: The first index is 0; index 1 is the second item.

commonMistakes.claim: other = items creates an independent copy.
commonMistakes.correction: Both names refer to one list. Use copy() for the simple one-level lists in this lesson.

practice.problem: What is the first item in [10, 20]?
Append 30 to [10, 20], then print each item.

answer.code:
values = [10, 20]
values.append(30)
for value in values:
    print(value)

values = [2, 3, 4]
total = 0
for value in values:
    total = total + value
print(total)

practice.problem: Copy [1, 2] and append 3 only to the copy. How long is the original?
solution: The copy has three items; the original still has two.

answer.code:
values = [1, 2]
other = values.copy()
other.append(3)
print(len(values))
print(len(other))

learningCheck.question: Which index reads the first shopping-list item?
feedback: Yes. Index 0 is the first item.
The length is one greater than the last valid index, so it is out of range.
